sanskrit: muner vacanam aklībaṃ śrutvā naravarātmajaḥ rāghavaḥ prāñjalir bhūtvā pratyuvāca dṛḍhavrataḥ
english: Having heard the sage's spirited, undaunted command, the son of the best of men, Rāghava, stood with palms joined and replied—he who was firm in his vow.

sanskrit: pitur vacananirdeśāt pitur vacanagauravāt vacanaṃ kauśikasyeti kartavyam aviśaṅkayā
english: "By the direction of my father's words, out of reverence for my father's command, the word of Kauśika (Viśvāmitra) must be carried out without any hesitation."

sanskrit: anuśiṣṭo 'smy ayodhyāyāṃ gurumadhye mahātmanā pitrā daśarathenāhaṃ nāvajñeyaṃ ca tad vacaḥ
english: "I have been instructed in Ayodhyā, in the assembly of elders, by my noble-souled father Daśaratha himself—and his word is not to be disregarded."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ pitur vacaḥ śrutvā śāsanād brahma vādinaḥ kariṣyāmi na saṃdehas tāṭakāvadham uttamam
english: "Therefore I, having heard my father's word and acting under the command of you who speak the truth of Brahman, will slay Tāṭakā—of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: gobrāhmaṇahitārthāya deśasyāsya sukhāya ca tava caivāprameyasya vacanaṃ kartum udyataḥ
english: "For the welfare of cows and brāhmaṇas, for the happiness of this region, and to fulfill the command of you who are immeasurable—I am ready to act."

sanskrit: evam uktvā dhanurmadhye baddhvā muṣṭim ariṃdamaḥ jyāśabdam akarot tīvraṃ diśaḥ śabdena pūrayan
english: Having spoken thus, the subduer of foes gripped his bow in the middle and made the bowstring resound with a fierce twang that filled all the quarters with its sound.

sanskrit: tena śabdena vitrastās tāṭakā vanavāsinaḥ tāṭakā ca susaṃkruddhā tena śabdena mohitā
english: By that sound the forest-dwellers were terrified and Tāṭakā herself was greatly enraged—bewildered by that sound.

sanskrit: taṃ śabdam abhinidhyāya rākṣasī krodhamūrchitā śrutvā cābhyadravad vegād yataḥ śabdo viniḥsṛtaḥ
english: Concentrating on that sound, the rākṣasī, overcome with fury, rushed with great speed toward the direction from which the sound had issued.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā rāghavaḥ kruddhāṃ vikṛtāṃ vikṛtānanām pramāṇenātivṛddhāṃ ca lakṣmaṇaṃ so 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Seeing her—enraged, misshapen, disfigured of face, and of enormous stature—Rāghava spoke to Lakṣmaṇa:

sanskrit: paśya lakṣmaṇa yakṣiṇyā bhairavaṃ dāruṇaṃ vapuḥ bhidyeran darśanād asyā bhīrūṇāṃ hṛdayāni ca
english: "Look, Lakṣmaṇa, at the terrible and fearsome form of this yakṣī—the hearts of the faint-hearted would shatter at the mere sight of her."

sanskrit: enāṃ paśya durādharṣāṃ māyā balasamanvitām vinivṛttāṃ karomy adya hṛtakarṇāgranāsikām
english: "See how formidable she is, endowed with the power of illusion. Today I will render her harmless by severing her ears and the tip of her nose."

sanskrit: na hy enām utsahe hantuṃ strīsvabhāvena rakṣitām vīryaṃ cāsyā gatiṃ cāpi haniṣyāmīti me matiḥ
english: "I cannot bring myself to kill her—for she is protected by the nature of womanhood. My intention is only to cripple her valor and her movement."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇe rāme tu tāṭakā krodhamūrchitā udyamya bāhū garjantī rāmam evābhyadhāvata
english: While Rāma was speaking thus, Tāṭakā, frenzied with rage, raised her arms and roaring rushed straight at Rāma.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ vegena vikrāntām aśanīm iva śareṇorasi vivyādha sā papāta mamāra ca
english: As she charged with terrifying speed, like a thunderbolt, he pierced her in the chest with an arrow. She fell and died.

sanskrit: tāṃ hatāṃ bhīmasaṃkāśāṃ dṛṣṭvā surapatis tadā sādhu sādhv iti kākutsthaṃ surāś ca samapūjayan
english: Seeing her slain—she who had the appearance of one inspiring dread—the lord of the gods then cried "Bravo! Bravo!" and the gods honored Kākutstha (Rāma).

sanskrit: uvāca paramaprītaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ puraṃdaraḥ surāś ca sarve saṃhṛṣṭā viśvāmitram athābruvan
english: Purandara (Indra), the thousand-eyed, spoke with the utmost delight, and all the gods, rejoicing greatly, then addressed Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: mune kauśike bhadraṃ te sendrāḥ sarve marudgaṇāḥ toṣitāḥ karmaṇānena snehaṃ darśaya rāghave
english: "O sage Kauśika, good fortune to you! All the troops of Maruts together with Indra are satisfied by this deed. Show your affection for Rāghava."

sanskrit: prajāpater kṛśāśvasya putrān satyaparākramān tapobalabhṛtān brahman rāghavāya nivedaya
english: "Reveal to Rāghava, O brahmin, the sons of Prajāpati Kṛśāśva—those of true valor, endowed with the might of austerity."

sanskrit: pātrabhūtaś ca te brahmaṃs tavānugamane dhṛtaḥ kartavyaṃ ca mahat karma surāṇāṃ rājasūnunā
english: "This son of a king, who is engaged in accompanying you, O brahmin, is worthy of them; and there is a great deed for the gods that the prince must accomplish."

sanskrit: evam uktvā surāḥ sarve hṛṣṭā jagmur yathāgatam viśvāmitraṃ pūjayitvā tataḥ saṃdhyā pravartate
english: Having spoken thus, all the gods, delighted, departed as they had come, after honoring Viśvāmitra; then twilight set in.

sanskrit: tato munivaraḥ prītis tāṭakā vadhatoṣitaḥ mūrdhni rāmam upāghrāya idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then the best of sages, filled with joy and satisfied by the slaying of Tāṭakā, sniffed Rāma's crown in affection and spoke these words:

sanskrit: ihādya rajanīṃ rāma vasema śubhadarśana śvaḥ prabhāte gamiṣyāmas tad āśramapadaṃ mama
english: "Let us spend this night here, O Rāma of auspicious appearance; at dawn tomorrow we shall go to that hermitage of mine."

sanskrit: atha tāṃ rajanīm uṣya viśvāmiro mahāyaśāḥ prahasya rāghavaṃ vākyam uvāca madhurākṣaram
english: Having passed that night, the greatly renowned Viśvāmitra smiled and spoke sweet-syllabled words to Rāghava.

sanskrit: patituṣṭo 'smi bhadraṃ te rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ prītyā paramayā yukto dadāmy astrāṇi sarvaśaḥ
english: "I am satisfied in my master, O greatly renowned prince of good fortune. Filled with the highest affection, I grant you all the weapons entirely."

sanskrit: devāsuragaṇān vāpi sagandharvoragān api yair amitrān prasahyājau vaśīkṛtya jayiṣyasi
english: "By these weapons you will, by force, bring enemies under control in battle and conquer the hosts of gods and asuras, together with gandharvas and serpents."

sanskrit: tāni divyāni bhadraṃ te dadāmy astrāṇi sarvaśaḥ daṇḍacakraṃ mahad divyaṃ tava dāsyāmi rāghava
english: "I grant you all those divine weapons—good fortune to you. The great and divine Daṇḍacakra I shall give to you, Rāghava."

sanskrit: dharmacakraṃ tato vīra kālacakraṃ tathaiva ca viṣṇucakraṃ tathātyugram aindraṃ cakraṃ tathaiva ca
english: "Then, O hero, the Dharmacakra and likewise the Kālacakra; the Viṣṇucakra, which is extremely fierce, and likewise the Indracakra."

sanskrit: vajram astraṃ naraśreṣṭha śaivaṃ śūlavaraṃ tathā astraṃ brahmaśiraś caiva aiṣīkam api rāghava dadāmi te mahābāho brāhmam astram anuttamam
english: "The Vajra weapon, O best of men, and likewise Śiva's excellent Śūla; the Brahmaśiras weapon, and also the Aiṣīka, O Rāghava—I give to you, O mighty-armed one, the incomparable Brāhma weapon."

sanskrit: gade dve caiva kākutstha modakī śikharī ubhe pradīpte naraśārdūla prayacchāmi nṛpātmaja
english: "Two maces also, O Kākutstha—Modakī and Śikharī, both blazing—I bestow upon you, O tiger among men, son of a king."

sanskrit: dharmapāśam ahaṃ rāma kālapāśaṃ tathaiva ca vāruṇaṃ pāśam astraṃ ca dadāny aham anuttamam
english: "The Dharmapāśa, O Rāma, and likewise the Kālapāśa, and also the incomparable Vāruṇa noose-weapon—these I give you."

sanskrit: aśanī dve prayacchāmi śuṣkārdre raghunandana
english: "Two thunderbolts I bestow upon you, O delight of the Raghu clan—one dry and one wet."

sanskrit: dadāmi cāstraṃ painākam astraṃ nārāyaṇaṃ tathā āgneyam astra dayitaṃ śikharaṃ nāma nāmataḥ
english: "I give also the Pāinaka weapon, and likewise the Nārāyaṇa weapon; the dear Āgneya weapon named Śikhara by name."

sanskrit: vāyavyaṃ prathamaṃ nāma dadāmi tava rāghava astraṃ hayaśiro nāma krauñcam astraṃ tathaiva ca
english: "I give you the Vāyavya weapon named Prathama, O Rāghava; the weapon named Hayaśiras, and likewise the Krauñca weapon."

sanskrit: śakti dvayaṃ ca kākutstha dadāmi tava cānagha kaṅkālaṃ musalaṃ ghoraṃ kāpālam atha kaṅkaṇam
english: "Two Śaktis also, O Kākutstha, I give to you, O sinless one; the Kaṅkāla, the dreadful Musala, the Kāpāla, and the Kaṅkaṇa."

sanskrit: dhārayanty asurā yāni dadāmy etāni sarvaśaḥ vaidyādharaṃ mahāstraṃ ca nandanaṃ nāma nāmataḥ
english: "Those weapons which the asuras wield—all of these I give you entirely; and the great Vaidyādhara weapon, named Nandana by name."

sanskrit: asiratnaṃ mahābāho dadāmi nṛvarātmaja gāndharvam astraṃ dayitaṃ mānavaṃ nāma nāmataḥ
english: "A jewel-sword I give you, O mighty-armed son of the best of kings; and the dear Gāndharva weapon, named Mānava by name."

sanskrit: prasvāpanapraśamane dadmi sauraṃ ca rāghava darpaṇaṃ śoṣaṇaṃ caiva saṃtāpanavilāpane
english: "Prasvāpana and Praśamana I give, and also the Saura weapon, O Rāghava; Darpaṇa and Śoṣaṇa, and Saṃtāpana and Vilāpana."

sanskrit: madanaṃ caiva durdharṣaṃ kandarpadayitaṃ tathā paiśācam astraṃ dayitaṃ mohanaṃ nāma nāmataḥ pratīccha naraśārdūla rājaputra mahāyaśaḥ
english: "And Madana, which is irresistible and dear to Kandarpa (Kāma); the dear Paiśāca weapon, named Mohana by name—receive these, O tiger among men, O greatly renowned prince."

sanskrit: tāmasaṃ naraśārdūla saumanaṃ ca mahābalam saṃvartaṃ caiva durdharṣaṃ mausalaṃ ca nṛpātmaja
english: "Tāmasa, O tiger among men, and Saumana of great might; the irresistible Saṃvarta and Mausala, O son of a king."

sanskrit: satyam astraṃ mahābāho tathā māyādharaṃ param ghoraṃ tejaḥprabhaṃ nāma paratejo'pakarṣaṇam
english: "The Satya weapon, O mighty-armed one, and likewise the supreme Māyādhara; the dreadful weapon named Tejaḥprabha, which diminishes the radiance of enemies."

sanskrit: somāstraṃ śiśiraṃ nāma tvāṣṭram astraṃ sudāmanam dāruṇaṃ ca bhagasyāpi śīteṣum atha mānavam
english: "The Soma weapon named Śiśira; the Tvāṣṭra weapon Sudāmana; and the terrible weapon of Bhaga, Śīteṣu; then the Mānava."

sanskrit: etān nāma mahābāho kāmarūpān mahābalān gṛhāṇa paramodārān kṣipram eva nṛpātmaja
english: "These, O mighty-armed son of a king, that assume any form at will, of great power, supremely excellent—receive them quickly."

sanskrit: sthitas tu prāṅmukho bhūtvā śucir nivaratas tadā dadau rāmāya suprīto mantragrāmam anuttamam
english: Then, standing and facing east, in a state of purity and self-restraint, Viśvāmitra, deeply pleased, bestowed upon Rāma the incomparable collection of mantras.

sanskrit: japatas tu munes tasya viśvāmitrasya dhīmataḥ upatasthur mahārhāṇi sarvāṇy astrāṇi rāghavam
english: And while the wise sage Viśvāmitra recited the mantras, all those supremely worthy weapons presented themselves before Rāghava.

sanskrit: ūcuś ca muditā rāmaṃ sarve prāñjalayas tadā ime sma paramodāra kiṃkarās tava rāghava
english: And all of them, delighted, stood before Rāma with hands joined and spoke: "We are here, O supremely noble Rāghava—your servants."

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca kākutsthaḥ samālabhya ca pāṇinā manasā me bhaviṣyadhvam iti tāny abhyacodayat
english: Kākutstha, having received them and touched them with his hand, urged them on, saying: "Dwell in my mind."

sanskrit: tataḥ prītamanā rāmo viśvāmitraṃ mahāmunim abhivādya mahātejā gamanāyopacakrame
english: Then Rāma, with a joyful heart and of great splendor, having reverently saluted the great sage Viśvāmitra, prepared to proceed on the journey.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tato 'strāṇi prahṛṣṭavadanaḥ śuciḥ gacchann eva ca kākutstho viśvāmitram athābravīt
english: Having received the weapons, Kākutstha, with a joyful face and in a state of purity, as he walked along spoke to Viśvāmitra:

sanskrit: gṛhītāstro 'smi bhagavan durādharṣaḥ surair api astrāṇāṃ tv aham icchāmi saṃhāraṃ munipuṃgava
english: "I have received the weapons, O blessed one, and am now unassailable even by the gods. But I desire also the withdrawal formulae for the weapons, O bull among sages."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvati kākutsthe viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ saṃhāraṃ vyājahārātha dhṛtimān suvrataḥ śuciḥ
english: As Kākutstha spoke thus, the great sage Viśvāmitra—steadfast, of excellent vows, and pure—then imparted the withdrawals.

sanskrit: satyavantaṃ satyakīrtiṃ dhṛṣṭaṃ rabhasam eva ca pratihārataraṃ nāma parāṅmukham avāṅmukham
english: Satyavat, Satyakīrti, Dhṛṣṭa, and Rabhasa; Pratihāratara by name, Parāṅmukha, and Avāṅmukha—

sanskrit: lakṣākṣaviṣamau caiva dṛḍhanābhasunābhakau daśākṣaśatavaktrau ca daśaśīrṣaśatodarau
english: Lakṣākṣa and Viṣama; Dṛḍhanābha and Sunābhaka; Daśākṣa and Śatavaktra; Daśaśīrṣa and Śatodara—

sanskrit: padmanābhamahānābhau dundunābhasunābhakau jyotiṣaṃ kṛśanaṃ caiva nairāśya vimalāv ubhau
english: Padmanābha and Mahānābha; Dundunābha and Sunābhaka; Jyotiṣa and Kṛśana; and the two—Nairāśya and Vimala—

sanskrit: yaugandharaharidrau ca daityapramathanau tathā pitryaṃ saumanasaṃ caiva vidhūtamakarāv ubhau
english: Yaugandhara and Haridra, and likewise Daityapramathana; Pitrya and Saumanasa; and the two—Vidhūtamakara—

sanskrit: karavīrakaraṃ caiva dhanadhānyau ca rāghava kāmarūpaṃ kāmaruciṃ moham āvaraṇaṃ tathā
english: And Karavīrakara; Dhana and Dhānya, O Rāghava; Kāmarūpa and Kāmaruci; Moha and Āvaraṇa—

sanskrit: jṛmbhakaṃ sarvanābhaṃ ca santānavaraṇau tathā kṛśāśvatanayān rāma bhāsvarān kāmarūpiṇaḥ
english: Jṛmbhaka and Sarvanābha; and Santāna and Varaṇa—these sons of Kṛśāśva, O Rāma, resplendent and capable of assuming any form at will—

sanskrit: pratīccha mama bhadraṃ te pātrabhūto 'si rāghava divyabhāsvaradehāś ca mūrtimantaḥ sukhapradāḥ
english: "Receive these from me—good fortune to you. You are worthy of them, O Rāghava. They are of divine and radiant form, embodied, and bestowers of bliss."

sanskrit: rāmaṃ prāñjalayo bhūtvābruvan madhurabhāṣiṇaḥ ime sma naraśārdūla śādhi kiṃ karavāma te
english: Standing before Rāma with hands joined, they spoke with sweet voices: "We are here, O tiger among men. Command us—what shall we do for you?"

sanskrit: gamyatām iti tān āha yatheṣṭaṃ raghunandanaḥ mānasāḥ kāryakāleṣu sāhāyyaṃ me kariṣyatha
english: The delight of the Raghu clan told them, "Go as you wish. Dwell in my mind, and at times of need you shall render me assistance."

sanskrit: atha te rāmam āmantrya kṛtvā cāpi pradakṣiṇam evam astv iti kākutstham uktvā jagmur yathāgatam
english: Then those weapons, taking leave of Rāma and circumambulating him, saying to Kākutstha "So be it," departed as they had come.

sanskrit: sa ca tān rāghavo jñātvā viśvāmitraṃ mahāmunim gacchann evātha madhuraṃ ślakṣṇaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: And Rāghava, knowing them to have departed, as he walked along then spoke sweet and gentle words to the great sage Viśvāmitra:

sanskrit: kiṃ nv etan meghasaṃkāśaṃ parvatasyāvidūrataḥ vṛkṣaṣaṇḍam ito bhāti paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: "What is that grove of trees, resembling a cloud, shining not far from the mountain? I am exceedingly curious about it."

sanskrit: darśanīyaṃ mṛgākīrṇaṃ manoharam atīva ca nānāprakāraiḥ śakunair valgubhāṣair alaṃkṛtam
english: "It is beautiful, filled with deer, exceedingly lovely, adorned with various kinds of birds of sweet song."

sanskrit: niḥsṛtāḥ sma muniśreṣṭha kāntārād romaharṣaṇāt anayā tv avagacchāmi deśasya sukhavattayā
english: "We have now emerged, O best of sages, from the hair-raising wilderness. By this I infer the pleasant nature of this region."

sanskrit: sarvaṃ me śaṃsa bhagavan kasyāśramapadaṃ tv idam saṃprāptā yatra te pāpā brahmaghnā duṣṭacāriṇaḥ
english: "Tell me everything, O blessed one—whose hermitage is this, where those sinful brahmin-slayers of wicked conduct came?"
